stoutford_widow_0.m: Please. Leave me alone. I'm mourning.
r: Is there anything I can do to ease your pain?

stoutford_widow_1.m: Oh. No one asked before you. I didn't even think about it.

stoutford_widow_10.m: Really? If you manage to do it, I'll make sure to reward you with something only I can do, and that I haven't done in a long time.
r: I guess I have work to do now.

stoutford_widow_11.m: That's a secret. I can't tell you, but you'll know when you'll see it.

stoutford_widow_12.m: Thank you for listening to me anyway. I wish you the best.

stoutford_widow_2.m: Are you willing to hear my story?
r: Oh no. Not a long story.
If it can be of any comfort ... go ahead.

stoutford_widow_3.m:
Thank you. My name is Aryfora.
I met my husband here in Stoutford, during the fair.
He offered me a beautiful flower, one that I had never seen before.

stoutford_widow_4.m:
He was smart and handsome and we quickly fell in love.
He was from a town called Remgard.
His name was Noraed.

stoutford_widow_5.m: He told me that it is very far from here, to the northeast, beyond the river and the mountains.

stoutford_widow_6.m: I've never been there, as he always said how dangerous that road was, but every year, for our anniversary, he went back to bring me a damerilia, the same flower he offered me on the day we met.

stoutford_widow_7.m:
During one of the recent attacks on Stoutford, my husband sacrificed his life to save mine.
Now, I can't do anything but mourn next to his grave.
r: He must have loved you very much.

stoutford_widow_8.m: I'd really love to place damerilias on his grave, as a symbol of our love.
r: Uh oh, I suspect I am going to be asked for something...

stoutford_widow_9.m: But it would be reckless of me to ask such a young kid as you to go so far to the northeast.
r: Don't worry about me. I can handle myself.
I'm an adventurer. I'm afraid of nothing.

stoutford_widow_roots10_0.m: You're back! Have you found some damerilias yet?
r: Yes. Here they are, three of the most beautiful damerilias.
Yes. Here they are, two of the most beautiful damerilias.
Yes. Here it is, the most beautiful one.

stoutford_widow_roots10_1.m: Oh. Come back to me if you find some, will you?

stoutford_widow_roots10_1a.m: Oh. But that is not enough - what would that look like! There must be at least 3 damerilias for the grave. Please...

stoutford_widow_roots10_2.m:
Oh. They're beautiful!
Thank you! Here, take this potion as your reward.

stoutford_widow_roots30_0.m: How did you find these flowers?
r: Caeda, Noraed's sister, gave them to me. She sends you her condolences.
I found them in the wild around Remgard.

stoutford_widow_roots30_1.m:
Is that so?
Remgard must be a beautiful place to have such nice flowers growing in the wild.
r: Beautiful, but deadly to get there!

stoutford_widow_roots30_3.m: Noraed had a sister? He never talked about his family. He said he had a happy childhood, but that's it. I think he didn't want me to ask to go there with him. I'd love to meet her someday.
r: I'm sure she feels the same.

stoutford_widow_roots4045_0.m: Thank you very much for the flowers. Is there anything I can do for you?
r: Your potion was great! Can I have some more?
That potion you made smells really interesting. Can I buy another?

stoutford_widow_roots4045_10.m: My uncle also convinced the whole village that I was too young to be their alchemist, and that they needed him to take over the shop.

stoutford_widow_roots4045_11.m:
They all agreed, even though my uncle is a lousy alchemist.
I was sent to work on a farm, while my uncle took my father's house and opened the shop again.

stoutford_widow_roots4045_12.m: Everyone suffered from the nasty side effects of my uncle's ... I can't say potions ... poisonous imitations of my father's recipes.

stoutford_widow_roots4045_13.m: People complained at first, but nobody ever looked for a real solution.

stoutford_widow_roots4045_14.m: Seeing how things turned out, I came to suspect that my uncle is responsible for my father's death.
r: And would you brew more potions if you had your father's shop back?

stoutford_widow_roots4045_15.m: No. Every time I talk to him, he denies everything, and calls me crazy. I can tell he's lying though.
r: And would you brew more potions if you had your father's shop back?

stoutford_widow_roots4045_16.m: Maybe. If the villagers asked me to, and if they recognize the guilt of my uncle.
r: Can I help you with this?

stoutford_widow_roots4045_16a.m: You have already done so much for me. I cannot accept that.

stoutford_widow_roots4045_17.m: Really? Then I think I have a plan.

stoutford_widow_roots4045_18.m: My uncle is very cautious with me, but with an unknown kid, there's a chance we can make him confess.

stoutford_widow_roots4045_19.m: He's a dangerous man though. Are you sure you wish to confront him?
r: Eh, I'd better leave now. It's none of my business.

stoutford_widow_roots4045_2.m: I gave you my last one, and I can't brew potions anymore.

stoutford_widow_roots4045_3.m: It is something I gave up long ago.

r: Never mind. Now I understand why Noraed traveled so far every year.

stoutford_widow_roots4045_5.m: My father was the alchemist of this town. He was very talented, and inspired. He experimented with all sorts of ingredients from all over Dhayavar. Whatever he could get from the travellers stopping at Stoutford.

stoutford_widow_roots4045_6.m: He created unique potions, and no other alchemist that I have heard of managed to reproduce his recipes.

stoutford_widow_roots4045_7.m: When he deemed me old and responsible enough, he started teaching me his art.

stoutford_widow_roots4045_8.m: He passed away a few years later. They said he poisoned himself during a new experiment, but I never believed it.
r: Sorry, I have to go now.

stoutford_widow_roots4045_9.m: Our priest, Tahalendor, was convinced by my uncle, Blornvale, my father's own brother.

stoutford_widow_thorns10_0.m:
To begin, you'll have to buy some potions of the brave from him. I need these as the base for a potion I want to create.
Don't forget: three potions of the brave.
r: What will you do with them?

stoutford_widow_thorns10_1.m: The potion of the brave can be enhanced to the much more useful potion of truth. These additions are easy, but for the potion of the brave I would need a laboratory.

stoutford_widow_thorns10_2.m: That is why you must get the potions of the brave from Blornvale. Oh how I hate that name! Be quick.
r: By chance, I have three potions of the brave with me. Here, take them.

stoutford_widow_thorns20_0.m: Did you get the three potions of the brave from Blornvale?
r: Yes, I have them. But I won't give them to you.

stoutford_widow_thorns20_1.m: Great! This will finally break him.
r: I hope so. He is a most unfriendly guy.

stoutford_widow_thorns20_2.m: What? Do you betray me? We must get rid of Blornvale!
r: I don't quit think so. He is an honest person.
I'm just kidding. Here, take the three potions.

stoutford_widow_thorns20_4.m: I would not have expected that from you!

stoutford_widow_thorns20_5.m: Aryfora just glares at you. Her eyes are icy cold.

stoutford_widow_thorns30_0.m:
Now I take three potions of the brave *chanting* ... add my prepared ingredients *chanting* ... shake it *chanting* ... shake it - ready.
Here, be careful with it. Potions of truth are rare.
r: Thank you. What do you have in mind now?

stoutford_widow_thorns40_0.m: With the potion of truth you will make Blornvale confess that he poisoned his brother.
r: But who would believe me, a stranger?

stoutford_widow_thorns40_1.m: You are right. We need a credible witness...

stoutford_widow_thorns40_2.m: Best would be Tahalendor himself. Yes, you must persuade the priest to be present when Blornvale tells the whole story.
r: Tahalendor? How can I do that?

stoutford_widow_thorns40_3.m: I have full confidence in you. You will come up with something.

stoutford_widow_thorns50_0.m: Did Blornvale drink the potion of truth?

stoutford_widow_thorns70_0.m: Did Blornvale drink the potion of truth?
r: Yes. I just have to make him confess to the murder.
Yes, he confessed to poisoning your father.
Yes, but it's not good news. Tahalendor won't believe me.
Yes, but it's not good news. He guessed that I tried to entrap him, and is cautious now.

stoutford_widow_thorns74_1.m: Oh no! Now I will never get justice!

stoutford_widow_thorns80_0.m: You look like you are in a good mood. What did you accomplish?
r: Blornvale is gone! Tahalendor came to hear him give a detailed confession to the murder. Then he took him away.

stoutford_widow_thorns80_1.m: At last! How can I thank you?
r: Oh, that was just a trifle.
No problem. I can handle myself.

stoutford_widow_thorns80_2.m: Now I can move back into my father's house and create potions again. I will leave at once. Please come and visit me at any time.

nondisplay_2.75: Taret tells you to be more careful what you say

thorns_vengeance.10: Aryfora in Stoutford needs my help to prove her uncle, Blornvale, Stoutford's alchemist, killed her father.
thorns_vengeance.20: She needs me to purchase three potions of the brave from Blornvale and return to her.
thorns_vengeance.30: I have returned with the three potions, and gave them to her.
thorns_vengeance.32: I decided not to help Aryfora any further.
thorns_vengeance.40: She gave me a potion of truth.
thorns_vengeance.50: She wants me to give that potion to Blornvale, and make him confess his crimes. I should have Tahalendor as a witness.
thorns_vengeance.60: I agreed to make Blornvale drink that potion.
thorns_vengeance.65: Tahalendor agreed to go with me to the alchemist's house to hear Blornvale's confession.
thorns_vengeance.71: Tahalendor came to hear Blornvale's confession.
thorns_vengeance.72: Blornvale confessed to killing Aryfora's father. Unfortunately there is no witness.
thorns_vengeance.74: Blornvale now understands what I was trying to do. I will no longer be able to help Aryfora get back her shop.
thorns_vengeance.75: Tahalendor wouldn't believe my story. I will no longer be able to help Aryfora get back her shop.
thorns_vengeance.76: It's all my fault that Aryfora is crying now.
thorns_vengeance.80: Blornvale confessed to killing Aryfora's father in the presence of Tahalendor.

roots_love.10: Aryfora, a woman grieving in Stoutford's graveyard asked me to bring her some damerilias from Remgard for the grave of Noraed, her husband.
roots_love.20: Noraed's sister, Caeda, gave me some damerilias. I should bring them back to Stoutford.
roots_love.30: I have brought the damerilias back to Aryfora. She thanked me with a potion she made.
roots_love.40: I told her the flowers were from Noraed's sister, Caeda.
roots_love.45: I told her I found the flowers around Remgard, in the wild.
